title: Ponderosa (QAES Ch 0 4) chico: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Ponderosa (QAES Ch 0 4) chico is a chico variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Ponderosa (QAES Ch 0 4) is a registered chico variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1992. Quezon Agricultural Experiment Station bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Ponderosa (QAES Ch 0 4) chico is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [chico variety finder](/crop-varieties/chico), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about Ponderosa (QAES Ch 0 4) chico
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chico fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A fruit of Ponderosa (QAES Ch 0 4) weighs about 214.68 grams, and its shape is ovoid. The flesh is smooth and firm.
Where and when to plant Ponderosa (QAES Ch 0 4) chico

Pick a selection with big, sweet fruit and few seeds, and plant marcotted or grafted trees. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.
